item.title: U.S. Open door is wide open, and an American man must walk through it and win the title
item.description: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe meet in the U.S. Open semifinals with Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic all already eliminated.
item.content:encoded:
American men's tennis has run out of excuses.

World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew from the U.S. Open prior to the tournament with a knee injury. Then, Novak Djokovic lost in the first round.

Finally, in a stunning upset, Ben Shelton sent defending champion Carlos Alcaraz home after a five-set battle that ended at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday morning.

BEN SHELTON TAKES DOWN CARLOS ALCARAZ TO EARN THE BIGGEST WIN OF HIS CAREER IN LATEST US OPEN MATCH EVER

Now Shelton and Frances Tiafoe will meet in the semifinals on Friday, which guarantees that an American man will play for the U.S. Open championship on Sunday afternoon in Flushing.

That's nice, but it isn't enough. One of them needs to hoist the trophy.

Andy Roddick remains the last American man to win a Grand Slam singles title. He did it at the U.S. Open in 2003, which means the drought is well into its third decade.

We've spent more than 20 years searching for the next guy. There have been promising teenagers, big servers, top-10 players and a lot of perfectly respectable runs to the second week of major tournaments. But this is America, and we don't do "respectable." We do dominant.

Taylor Fritz reached the U.S. Open final in 2024. Tiafoe made the semifinals in 2022. Shelton got there in 2023. Those are all good runs. But American men have been living off close calls for long enough, and it's time to finish the job. There's arguably never been a better opening for it to happen.

The two best men's tennis players in the world aren't standing in the way. Sinner, the No. 1 player in the world and reigning Wimbledon champion, withdrew before the tournament with a right knee injury.

Alcaraz, the reigning Australian Open and U.S. Open champ, made it to New York after missing the past two majors with a wrist injury, but Shelton beat him. Djokovic's 39-year-old body betrayed him in a stunning first-round loss to Mariano Navone.

Alexander Zverev is still alive, and he finally got over the Grand Slam hump at the French Open earlier this year, in part due to Alcaraz's absence. He's a serious threat, but he's not at the level of either Sinner or Alcaraz, the two players who had combined to win nine straight major titles before Zverev broke through in Paris.

The remaining field has good players. It doesn't have an unbeatable one, and sometimes in tennis that's all you can ask for.

Shelton certainly didn't get a free pass into the semifinals. Alcaraz entered their quarterfinal with a 13-0 record against American men in Grand Slam matches.

Shelton dropped the first set in a tiebreak, then ripped through the next two to take control of the match. Alcaraz answered with a dominant fourth set, and more than four hours after they started, it came down to a deciding tiebreak.

LADIES AT THE US OPEN WERE CAUGHT ON CAMERA TAKING NOTICE OF A SHIRTLESS CARLOS ALCARAZ

Despite facing the most pressure-packed moments of his career, Shelton came through to beat the 23-year-old Spaniard. Shelton has had plenty of near misses, which made this victory feel like a breakthrough.

The power has never been in doubt. His serve is a weapon, his athleticism jumps off the screen and he feeds off an enthusiastic crowd better than almost anyone on tour.

But could he beat one of the sport's giants when the match was on the line and the lights shone their brightest? Finally, that answer is a resounding yes.

Tiafoe had to answer a different question. He fell behind fellow American Alex Michelsen by two sets and a break in their quarterfinal and was staring at a quiet exit after squandering a golden opportunity.

Things looked especially bleak because Michelsen hadn't dropped a single set in the tournament up to that point.

Tiafoe could have folded, especially after all the years of people waiting for him to turn his talent into a major title. Instead, he fought his way back and won in a fifth-set tiebreak.

Tiafoe is 28. He's not old, but he's not the young prospect with unlimited time anymore. This is his third trip to a major semifinal, all at the U.S. Open. At some point, the breakthrough has to become more than making it to Friday night.

And Tiafoe knows it.

"We're going to enjoy this, but we got to keep going," he said after beating Michelsen.

Shelton is 23 and probably has more opportunities ahead of him. But ask Dan Marino how many more Super Bowl appearances he thought he'd have after he made his first one at 23. The answer was zero.

There will be plenty of talk about how great Friday's semifinal is for American tennis, and it is. Arthur Ashe Stadium will be packed and fired up to watch two American stars with big personalities, huge games and a real chance to end a 23-year major-title drought.

But the celebration can't peak in the semifinal.

We already know an American can reach the final. Fritz did it two years ago, then Sinner beat him in straight sets. Getting another man to the last Sunday would show consistency. Winning could change the sport in this country.

That may sound dramatic, but look around. American women's tennis has continued producing major champions. Coco Gauff, Madison Keys and Sofia Kenin have all won Grand Slam singles titles in this decade. The men keep giving fans encouraging signs and asking them to wait a little longer.

We can't wait much longer.

Whoever wins between Shelton and Tiafoe will have the New York crowd, a winnable final and the opportunity American men's tennis has spent 23 years trying to create. Sinner, Alcaraz and Djokovic are already gone. The last obstacle will be one very good player on one Sunday afternoon.

Many people probably want to already label this tournament as a success because an American man is guaranteed to at least make the final. I'm not one of them. At this point, it's victory or failure.

The door is open and it's time to finally walk through it.

item.title: Mel Gibson says 'monster' epic 'Passion' sequel spans spiritual realms — and this time, it's in English
item.description: Mel Gibson revealed why "The Resurrection of the Christ" ditches ancient languages for English and takes viewers on a spiritual journey across realms.
item.content:encoded:
Mel Gibson is ditching ancient languages for English in his upcoming two-part follow-up to "The Passion of the Christ," describing the new epic as a "trip" that will take moviegoers across spiritual realms.

Gibson spoke exclusively with Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo about his upcoming two-part follow-up, "The Resurrection of the Christ," including his decision to use English in the new films. 

The interview comes as the original 2004 film returns to theaters for a special Fathom Events re-release.

The full interview is featured on the "Arroyo Grande Show with Raymond Arroyo" YouTube channel.

'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' WRITER REVEALS MEL GIBSON'S DARK SPIRITUAL WARNING ABOUT 'PASSION' FOLLOW-UP

"You had a focal point, and it was about human suffering," Gibson said of the original film. "That was a rather simpler message to get across, and I think the complexity of an event like the resurrection, which is impossible to comprehend really, one has to delve more into sources.

"I thought it was just silly to make people read subtitles in a foreign language when they were dealing with such heady concepts. So, it asks more of you, but we help them along with their own language."

"The Passion of the Christ" is a biblical drama depicting the crucifixion of Jesus Christ in excruciating detail. It starred Jim Caviezel as Jesus and focused on the final 12 hours of Jesus’ life, with dialogue mainly in Aramaic, Hebrew and Latin.

MEL GIBSON'S 'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' REVEALS FIRST PHOTOS AFTER LONG-AWAITED PASSION SEQUEL

"The Resurrection of the Christ: Part One" is set for release May 6, 2027, with Part Two scheduled for May 25, 2028. While the original film focused on the final hours of Jesus’ life, Gibson said the new films will explore the resurrection and the days that followed.

Gibson said the upcoming films take viewers on a "trip" into other realms and explore how humanity is connected to them. He said the films are meant to show viewers the "big picture."

"It takes a pretty broad trip [from] our own broken world to, you know, other realms and stuff with different natures, and connects all of them, I hope — because we're all connected, and we all know we're connected," he said.

NEW BOOK ON ARCHAEOLOGICAL EVIDENCE FOR JESUS ROCKETS TO TOP OF BESTSELLER LIST

Gibson said the writing and pre-production process has taken more than a decade, and the new films are arriving over 20 years after the original premiered. He suggested the timing may be for a reason, saying, "There’s no accidents anywhere."

"I thought I was late. It was just too late, 23 years later, but it's probably just right. It's not my timing," Gibson said.

When asked whether he considers the project his own "resurrection" as a filmmaker, Gibson described the undertaking as a transformative, communal journey.

MEL GIBSON REVEALS ‘THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST’S’ MOST SURPRISING LEGACY IN NEW RAYMOND ARROYO INTERVIEW

"It’s a monster. It’s a massive undertaking," Gibson said. "I think, how can one not be changed by just being involved in that? And I didn't do it alone, either. There was a lot of people that came with me. So, it's a journey, right? That was a communal experience."

item.title: Minnesota Vikings surprisingly demote former first-round pick JJ McCarthy to third string
item.description: J.J. McCarthy dropped to third string as Carson Wentz was named backup behind starter Kyler Murray for the Vikings' Week 1 matchup vs. the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
J.J. McCarthy was once supposed to be "the guy" for the Minnesota Vikings. But going into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season, he's not even the guy's backup.

That's because Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell named Carson Wentz the team's backup quarterback for Sunday's home game against the Green Bay Packers.

And on Aug. 11, O’Connell named Kyler Murray the starter for Sunday’s game and the foreseeable future.

VIKINGS QB BATTLE MEETS EXPECTED END AS KYLER MURRAY STARTS OVER MCCARTHY

O’Connell told reporters Wentz would serve as the backup, and the team later released its depth chart, listing McCarthy behind him. Wentz was deemed more prepared to step in if Murray cannot play.

"I'm looking at that right now as a week-to-week thing," O'Connell said. "Carson, he's got almost 100 career starts. What he was able to do last year from the standpoint of very limited repetitions but being able to apply a career's worth of experience, that's kind of what you need to do as a backup quarterback — especially early on when so much of the emphasis is going to be on getting Kyler as comfortable as we can possibly get him.

"But J.J. is still going to get a bunch of great work..."

McCarthy's work will be mostly running some of the scout team for the Vikings, particularly during weeks they face a more mobile quarterback.

And that is a mighty fall for McCarthy, who was drafted in 2024 with expectations he would eventually be the team's franchise quarterback.

This announcement is merely the latest in a series of setbacks McCarthy has faced since the Vikings selected him No. 10 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

You’ll recall that the Vikings traded up to select McCarthy, passing on Bo Nix, who has since become Denver’s starter.

But McCarthy never played as a rookie after suffering a season-ending torn meniscus in his right knee during the Vikings’ first preseason game against the Raiders. That injury cost him an entire developmental year and left the team relying on Sam Darnold during a playoff season.

McCarthy finally became Minnesota’s starter in 2025, opening with an impressive fourth-quarter comeback at Chicago and earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.

But then things went sideways.

McCarthy struggled with turnovers and more injuries, including a concussion, and finished the season with 11 TD passes and 12 interceptions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The offseason also dealt McCarthy a blow because the Vikings didn't sit tight and bank on him developing into a good quarterback. They went out and found his replacement by adding Murray.

And this: If Murray plays well this year, as some believe he will, McCarthy may never get a chance to be the starter for the Vikings.

That’s because Murray will be a free agent after the season, and the Vikings aren’t about to repeat their Sam Darnold mistake. Darnold, you’ll recall, played well in 2024, but the Vikings didn’t re-sign him for 2025 and beyond despite his strong performance.

Darnold won the Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks last year.

The Vikings thus would likely re-sign Murray if he plays well.

And that would leave McCarthy a backup player for the rest of his time with the team, regardless of how rosy O'Connell paints things.

"I'm really excited to get a chance to continue to work with him," the coach said. "Want to make it week-to-week so when we need to declare something different, we can and we will. This gives us the best chance to win this Sunday."
